The second and last release candidate of v0.3.0. It fixes the AmneziaWG
profile that could not be created (A-286, also in v0.2.1 and rc.1) and a
sign-in check that let a token without an admin through (A-290), closes the
second wave of the audit, and adds an admin audit log with its screen and a
view of the users still connected to a node after they were taken off it.
sing-box now comes from its own repository. 56 commits since v0.3.0-rc.1.

This is a release candidate: run it on a stand or a node you can rebuild before
a production fleet. The installers still install v0.2.1 by default; to install
this candidate, set `ICESLAB_REF=v0.3.0-rc.2` for the panel and
`ICESLAB_NODE_REF=v0.3.0-rc.2` for a node.

## Known issue

On some mobile networks in Russia, REALITY on port 443 connects worse than
on a non-standard port; the same host on another port works there. Seen on the
stand, not caused by the panel. If clients on mobile data fail on a REALITY
host at 443, give that profile a second host on another port. The defaults are
reviewed for v0.3.0.

## Upgrading

Coming from v0.2.1, read the rc.1 notes first: everything they ask for once
(the `--caddy-only` step, the old connection lines, the old logs) still applies.
Coming from rc.1, update the panel and every node agent together, as root:

0. **Before the update, from v0.2.1 or rc.1: check six key names and one
   index name.** The migration `20261029064640_reconcile_drift` drops six
   foreign keys and renames one index by their exact names. A database where
   one of them carries another name stops that migration halfway through the
   update. From the compose root:
   ```
   docker exec -i iceslab-prod-postgres sh -c 'psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"' <<'SQL'
   select conname from pg_constraint where conname in (
     'amneziawg_peers_profile_id_fkey',
     'api_tokens_created_by_admin_id_fkey',
     'group_profiles_group_id_fkey',
     'group_profiles_profile_id_fkey',
     'profile_node_bindings_node_id_fkey',
     'profile_node_bindings_profile_id_fkey'
   ) order by 1;
   select indexname from pg_indexes
     where indexname = 'cascade_links_cascade_id_from_to_direction_key';
   SQL
   ```
   The first query answers all six names, the second the one index. If any
   name is missing, do not update: open an issue at
   https://github.com/icecompany-tech/iceslab/issues with the output of both
   queries.
1. **Panel**, from the compose root (usually `/opt/iceslab`):
   `ICESLAB_REF=v0.3.0-rc.2 ./scripts/ops/deploy.sh`.
2. **Every node agent**, over SSH. Do not run the node installer again (it
   issues a new mTLS pair):
   ```
   cd /opt/iceslab-node && git fetch --tags origin && git checkout --force v0.3.0-rc.2
   cd apps/node && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=$(git describe --tags --always)" -o /usr/local/bin/iceslab-node .
   systemctl restart iceslab-node
   ```
   The build needs Go 1.27.3, as for rc.1.

Six migrations run with the panel update:

- `20261026100207_deleted_node_secrets` clears the secrets of nodes deleted
  before (see Nodes). It changes no schema and has no data rollback: what it
  clears is gone.
- `20261027034521_admin_audit_events` adds the audit log table. Its rollback is
  in the file's header.
- `20261027041625_drop_inbounds` drops the `inbounds` and `group_inbounds`
  tables, unused since profiles replaced them. Its rollback, in the file's
  header, brings the tables back empty: their content has lived in profiles and
  bindings since then.
- `20261027070348_admin_audit_wave2` adds the network a sign-in came from to
  the audit log and an index for a user's history. Rollback, in the header:
  drop the index `admin_audit_events_detail_idx` and the column
  `source_network`.
- `20261029063532_audit_login_summary_unique` adds a unique index that keeps
  one summary row of refused sign-ins per hour and key (A-288). Rollback, in
  the header: drop the index `admin_audit_events_login_summary_key`.
- `20261029064640_reconcile_drift` brings six foreign keys and one index name
  to the shape the schema describes (see step 0). The keys gain
  `ON UPDATE CASCADE`; they are uuids nothing updates, so the behaviour does
  not change. The file runs as one transaction and holds each table's lock
  until it ends, so the check of the key on `amneziawg_peers` (a row per user
  and AmneziaWG profile) keeps that table locked while it reads it; the
  header's word that `NOT VALID` lightens the lock does not hold inside one
  file. Rollback, in the header: the six keys back without
  `ON UPDATE CASCADE`, and the index back to its old name.

Each rollback also removes the migration's row from `_prisma_migrations`, as
its header says.

## sing-box from core-builds

The panel's own sing-box 1.13.14 build, which per-user traffic on every
sing-box protocol needs, is now published in
[icecompany-tech/core-builds](https://github.com/icecompany-tech/core-builds)
under the same tag, `core-singbox-v1.13.14`, with its own signing key
(`keys/cores.pub` there). The archives are the same files, byte for byte, with
the same sha256, so a node that already has it changes nothing.

The old release of that build in this repository stays until v0.3.0, and the
rc.1 tag, which fetches sing-box from there, keeps installing nodes until then.
It is removed with v0.3.0.

## Profiles

- **A new AmneziaWG profile can be created again** (A-286). The form sent an
  empty H1..H4 header as 0, which the server refuses, so the save failed. The
  form now opens with four random distinct headers, refuses an empty, low or
  repeated one on its field before sending, and marks the field the server
  refused, if it does. Each H field now says what H takes.
- **The profile card shows each protocol's settings** (AmneziaWG, Hysteria,
  Xray and the rest) instead of a dash where the value sits deeper in the
  config (A-287).
- **Every key of a profile config has an owner** (A-285): the form sends it,
  the server keeps it, or the push sets it, and the list lives in the shared
  package. Tests hold each protocol's config schema to that list, and a fully
  filled form of every protocol to the keys it sends, so a key the form drops
  on save fails CI instead of reaching a release. Nothing changes on screen.
- **A Hysteria port hopping range needs both ends, and its end above its
  start** (A-284), on create and on edit. A range with one end used to be
  dropped without a word; the form and the server now refuse it on the field,
  in the same words.

## Nodes

- **Users still connected after they were taken off a node** (A-218). When a
  user is taken off a node, Xray refuses their new connections but lets the
  open ones run. The node's System block now lists those
  users, and the user's drawer names the nodes where they are still connected.
  This needs the rc.2 agent on Xray nodes; with an older agent, or on another
  core, the panel says "not checked" and never "nobody".
- **The Hysteria certificate line shows when the ACME certificate ends,** as
  the agent reads it from Hysteria's storage. With an older agent, or no
  certificate there yet, it reads "expiry unknown".
- **A Hysteria process still on the old log level is restarted once** on the
  next agent start, where an earlier restart did not take.
- **A deleted node keeps only what its agent's refusal needs** (A-279): its id
  and heartbeat secret, so the old agent is told 410. The chain password, the
  self-signed pair, the WARP credentials and the key material go with the
  delete, and the migration clears them from nodes deleted before.
- **A saved or deleted node policy refreshes the node page and its drawing**
  (A-283). The squad screen names a node policy rule that leads into a narrowed
  cascade only when it can tell, and says so when it cannot.

## Sign-in

- **A session token must name an admin** (A-290). A token signed with the
  panel's JWT secret but without an admin id in `sub` was let in as the first
  live admin: the lookup dropped the missing id and matched any row. Such a
  token is now refused with 401 before any lookup, and the lookup goes by key.
  The panel itself always signs its sessions with the admin's id, so only a
  holder of `JWT_SECRET` could make such a token; if yours may have left your
  hands, rotate it.

## Admin audit log

The panel keeps who deleted a user, cleared a node's log, rotated a node's
certificate, or changed a cascade or a node policy, with how it ended: done,
refused with its code, or failed. The admin is named in full; the user is
named masked. No token, key, password, request body or address is kept.

It also keeps sign-ins, with the network they came from (IPv4 /24 or IPv6
/48, never the address; behind a proxy the panel does not trust, the proxy's
network), the first admin's registration, turning the second factor on and
off, API tokens created and revoked with their scopes, panel settings by the
names whose value changed, and a bulk action on users as one row that each
user it reached finds in their history. An action by an API token is labelled
with the token's name. Refused sign-ins are written up to 20 an hour from one
network and 300 an hour in all; past that they are counted in one summary row
per hour for the network, or for all when the total is past (A-288), so
guessing from many addresses does not write a row per guess. A successful
sign-in and a refusal that locks an account are always written, and sign-in
itself is not limited by this.

The **Activity log** screen, under Tools (`/audit`), reads it: who did what to
which object and how it ended, with each action's detail, filtered by action,
object and period. It is an admin's screen, like the API below.

`GET /api/audit` reads it back with filters and a cursor, for an admin session
only: an API token gets `403 AUDIT_ADMIN_ONLY`. Entries are kept for 365 days.

## API

- `/api/inbounds` and the `inbounds:read` / `inbounds:write` token scopes are
  gone. The routes had answered nothing since profiles replaced inbounds; a
  token minted with the scope keeps it on its row, and it grants nothing. A new
  token with it is refused with 400.

## Panel

- The panel's Content Security Policy is enforced on its own pages. The
  subscription page and its preview run under a policy of their own, with a
  per-request nonce.
- The browser tab shows the Iceslab mark.

## Installers

- **The README's install command installs what it says** (A-282, already on
  `main`). Each installer now hands over to the installer of the ref it
  installs before it touches anything, so the command from `main` no longer
  runs one version's steps over another version's tree. `ICESLAB_HANDOVER=off`
  turns the handover off.

## For contributors

- The Prisma schema now describes the database as the migrations build it
  (defaults, the A-150 backup tables), and CI fails when the migrations and
  the schema part.
- `typecheck` of the backend also checks `scripts/` against the code they
  import (A-291), and the scale seeder runs on a fresh database and tops up on
  a second run (A-289).

## Dependencies

- `undici` 8.12.3, `@tanstack/react-query` 5.104.5, `typescript-eslint` 8.72.0
  (#53); `pnpm/action-setup` 6.1.0 in CI (#52).
